subject: Information Theory
title: Packet Switching
description: A quick, practical guide to Packet Switching.

hook.text: Your email doesn't travel as one piece. It's broken into packets that take different routes and reassemble at the end.

buildup.text: Packet switching divides data into small chunks. Each packet is routed independently through the network.

discovery.text: This is statistically multiplexed: many users share the same links. Packets interleave, maximizing utilization.

twist.text: Before packets, there was circuit switching: a dedicated line for each call. It wasted capacity when no one was talking.

climax.text: Baran and Davies independently invented packet switching in the 1960s. It became the foundation of the internet.

punchline.text: Break it into packets. Share the roads. That's the internet.

quiz.question: What advantage does packet switching have over circuit switching?
options: Many users share links efficiently through statistical multiplexing
